event.description: Prune two lowest-salience feed-forward units per block
event.proposal: Family: feed-forward width. Current retained frontier is 2,656 parameters at 99.980000%, a +0.980000 percentage-point margin over 99%. There have been 11 prior attempts in this family. The most recent accepted in-family result is attempt-0022, projection-free width 10 at 3,040 parameters and 99.85%; the most recent failed in-family result is attempt-0023, width 9, an optimization failure peaking at 98.35% internal validation. Attempt-0026 has since established a shared-QKV architecture at width 16 and 99.98%. Hypothesis: its larger feed-forward paths contain removable units; rank each unit by the product of its incoming-row and outgoing-column norms, then retain 14 of 16 independently per block. This checkpoint-derived, parameterization-preserving reduction yields 2,528 parameters and isolates functional redundancy from training noise. It is more informative than the nearest untested width 15 because removing two units is the smallest material step that tests whether the new architecture's large margin corresponds to redundant nonlinear channels.
